note: Every value is copied from the cited table or sentence as published. Nothing is rounded, combined or extrapolated.

stechly2024.title: On the Self-Verification Limitations of Large Language Models on Reasoning and Planning Tasks
stechly2024.authors: Kaya Stechly, Karthik Valmeekam, Subbarao Kambhampati
stechly2024.where: Table 1, arXiv HTML v2: 'Accuracy across prompting schemes over 100 instances per domain.' Model: GPT-4.
stechly2024.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license (values redrawn from the table, no figure copied)
stechly2024.conditions: GPT-4, 100 instances per domain. 'LLM+LLM' is GPT-4 critiquing its own answers; 'LLM+Sound Critique, B.F.' is a sound program checker giving binary feedback, not a second language model.

huang2024.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
huang2024.where: Table 3, arXiv HTML v2: 'Results of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on reasoning benchmarks with intrinsic self-correction.'
huang2024.conditions: Intrinsic self-correction: the model reviews its own answer with no external feedback.

panickssery2024.title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
panickssery2024.authors: Arjun Panickssery, Samuel R. Bowman, Shi Feng
panickssery2024.where: Introduction, finding 2: 'GPT-4 is 73.5% accurate distinguishing itself from two other LLMs and humans.'
panickssery2024.conditions: Summarization (XSUM, CNN/DailyMail), out of the box, no fine-tuning. Measures recognizing its own authorship, not review accuracy.

goel2025.title: Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines AI Oversight
goel2025.where: Section 3.2: 'a significant (p < 0.01) positive correlation (average Pearson r=0.84) between LLM-as-a-judge scores and model similarity'. Figure 6 caption: 'LM mistakes are getting more correlated with increasing capabilities'.
goel2025.conditions: Similarity measured by CAPA (overlap in mistakes). The capability trend has no single published coefficient. Cross-sectional across current models, not a trend over time; CAPA adjusts for chance agreement.

metr2026.title: Many SWE-bench-Passing PRs Would Not Be Merged into Main
metr2026.authors: Parker Whitfill, Cheryl Wu, Joel Becker, Nate Rush (METR)
metr2026.where: Summary: 4 active maintainers from 3 SWE-bench Verified repositories reviewed 296 AI-generated PRs; 'roughly half of test-passing SWE-bench Verified PRs' would not be merged, 'even after adjusting for noise in maintainer merge decisions'. Main results: grader averages about 24.2 percentage points (SE 2.7) above the maintainer merge decision.
metr2026.license: (c) 2026 METR, all rights reserved; facts quoted with attribution, nothing reproduced
metr2026.conditions: scikit-learn, Sphinx, pytest; agents from mid-2024 to late 2025, mostly Anthropic models; scores normalized to the golden-patch merge rate (about 68%); maintainers had no CI.

laban2025.title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
laban2025.authors: Philippe Laban, Hiroaki Hayashi, Yingbo Zhou, Jennifer Neville
laban2025.where: Abstract: 'with an average drop of 39% across six generation tasks'. Introduction: '15 LLMs'. (Figure 1 caption says -35%; the README uses the abstract's figure.)
laban2025.conditions: Simulated sharded (multi-turn) vs fully specified single-turn instructions; six generation tasks. Applies to simulated multi-turn tasks, not long chats in general.

cemri2025.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
cemri2025.where: Section 4 (FC1): 'improving agent role specifications alone yields a +9.4% success rate increase for ChatDev' 'with the same user prompt and LLM (GPT-4o)'.
cemri2025.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (fact quoted with attribution, nothing reproduced)
cemri2025.conditions: ChatDev on ProgramDev. Not used: a ~75% ChatDev failure rate and a +14% figure, which were not found in the text. Table 5 (ChatDev, ProgramDev-v0): 25.0% baseline and 34.4% with the improved role prompts; Section 4 (FC1) states the gain, so +9.4% is percentage points. Table 5 cells were confirmed in the PR's blind check.

kamoi2024.title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
kamoi2024.where: Abstract: 'self-correction works well in tasks that can use reliable external feedback'.

sharma2023.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
sharma2023.where: Section 3.2: 'Claude 1.3 wrongly admits mistakes on 98% of questions.' Section 3.3: 'The user suggesting an incorrect answer can reduce accuracy by up to 27% (LLaMA 2; Fig. 3).'
sharma2023.conditions: Five assistants: claude-1.3, claude-2.0, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, llama-2-70b-chat.
